'''Andrzej Bobola Maria Schinzel''' (5 April 1937<ref>{{cite book |chapter=Preface |chapter-url=http://www.ems-ph.org/books/053/preface_978-3-03719-038-8.pdf |title=Andrzej Schinzel, Selecta |volume=1 |editor1=H. Iwaniec |editor2=W. Narkiewicz |editor3=J. Urbanowicz |year=2007 |doi=10.4171/038 |isbn=978-3-03719-038-8 |mr=2383194 |zbl=1115.11002 |access-date=5 May 2010 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304055614/http://www.ems-ph.org/books/053/preface_978-3-03719-038-8.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> – 21 August 2021<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pożegnanie prof. dr hab. Andrzeja Schinzla (5 kwietnia 1937, Sandomierz – 21 sierpnia 2021, Konstancin)|url=https://sandomierz.eu/2667/pozegnanie-prof-dr-hab-andrzeja-schinzla-5-kwietnia-1937-sandomierz-21-sierpnia-2021-konstancin.html|access-date=5 September 2021|website=sandomierz.eu}}</ref>) was a Polish [[mathematician]] who specialised predominantly in [[number theory]].

[[File:WithProf.AndrzejSchinzel.jpg|thumb|Schinzel and Adam Grygiel in 2010]]

== Education ==
Schinzel earned an [[MSc]] in 1958 from [[Warsaw University]] and a [[Ph.D.]] in 1960 from the Institute of Mathematics of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] where he studied under [[Wacław Sierpiński]],<ref name=phd>{{MathGenealogy|id=52979}}</ref> with a [[habilitation]] in 1962. He was a member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stettner |first1=Łukasz |date=Autumn 2021 |title=Obituary: Andrzej Schinzel (1937-2021) |url=https://impan.pl/images/newsletter/newsletter_14_2021.pdf |journal=Newsletter- Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences |volume= |issue=14 |publisher=Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences |pages=4-5 }}</ref>

== Career ==
Schinzel was a professor at the Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences (IM PAN). His principal interest was the theory of [[polynomial]]s. His 1958 conjecture on the prime values of polynomials, known as [[Schinzel's hypothesis H]], both extends the [[Bunyakovsky conjecture]] and broadly generalizes the [[twin prime conjecture]]. He also proved [[Schinzel's theorem]] on the existence of [[circle]]s through any given number of integer points.

Schinzel authored over 200 research articles in various branches of number theory, including [[elementary number theory|elementary]], [[analytic number theory|analytic]] and [[algebraic number theory]]. He served as the editor of ''[[Acta Arithmetica]]'' for over four decades.

Schinzel collaborated with many colleagues, including [[Paul Erdős]] and [[Barbara Rokowska]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Szajowski |first1=Krzysztof |title=Barbara Rokowska's combinatorial research with her extensive biography (1926–2012) |journal=Antiq. Math. |date=2024 |volume=18 |pages=191–218}}</ref>

== Private life ==
Andrzej Schinzel was the elder brother of Polish [[chess master]] [[Władysław Schinzel]] (born 1943).<ref>[https://sandomierz.eu/2667/pozegnanie-prof-dr-hab-andrzeja-schinzla-5-kwietnia-1937-sandomierz-21-sierpnia-2021-konstancin.html Pożegnanie prof. dr hab. Andrzeja Schinzla (5 kwietnia 1937, Sandomierz – 21 sierpnia 2021, Konstancin)]</ref>
